title: Grade 8 Science — Fri, May 22
description: Crop Production & Management — Day 5 of 5: Synthesis — full topic review
subject: science

questions.question: Classify: Rice / Wheat / Cotton / Maize / Mustard → Kharif or Rabi?
options: Rice, Cotton, Maize = Kharif; Wheat, Mustard = Rabi
Rice, Wheat = Kharif; Cotton, Mustard, Maize = Rabi
questions.explanation: Kharif (monsoon): rice, maize, cotton, soybean. Rabi (winter): wheat, mustard, gram, peas. Key distinction for Indian agriculture.

questions.question: Correct sequence of crop production practices:
options: Ploughing → Levelling → Sowing → Irrigation → Weeding → Fertilization → Harvesting → Threshing → Storage
questions.explanation: Complete sequence: Soil prep (plough, harrow, level) → Sow → Add manure/fertilizer → Irrigate → Weed → Protect from pests → Harvest → Thresh → Winnow → Dry → Store.

questions.question: A farmer notices yellow leaves on his crop. This could indicate:
options: Nitrogen deficiency (nitrogen promotes green leaf growth)
Both nitrogen deficiency and waterlogging possible
questions.explanation: Yellow leaves: nitrogen deficiency (most common — apply urea/manure) OR waterlogging (roots can't absorb nutrients). Diagnosis needed before treatment.

questions.question: Leguminous crops (like gram, pea, soybean) are used in crop rotation because:
options: They grow fast in any soil
They fix atmospheric nitrogen through root nodule bacteria (Rhizobium), enriching soil naturally
questions.explanation: Legumes + Rhizobium bacteria: fix N₂ from atmosphere → soil nitrates. After harvest, roots decompose and release nitrogen → next crop benefits. Natural, free fertilizer.

questions.question: Drip irrigation vs flood irrigation: which conserves more water and why?
options: Flood irrigation saves more water as it covers the whole field
Drip saves more — delivers water directly to roots with minimal evaporation and runoff
Sprinkler is best — drip and flood both waste water
questions.explanation: Flood irrigation: 30–40% water loss to evaporation/runoff. Drip: 90%+ efficiency — water goes directly to roots via pipes. Critical in water-scarce regions.

questions.question: Integrated Pest Management (IPM) — why is it better than only chemical pesticides?
options: IPM reduces resistance development, protects beneficial insects, less soil/water pollution, long-term effectiveness
IPM never works on large farms
questions.explanation: Chemical pesticides alone: pests develop resistance, kill beneficial insects (bees, ladybugs), pollute soil/water, harm humans. IPM combines biological, cultural, and chemical methods minimally.

questions.question: The Green Revolution solved India's food crisis but created some problems. Which?
options: No problems — it was purely beneficial
Groundwater depletion (excess irrigation), soil salinity, loss of crop diversity, chemical pollution, regional inequality
questions.explanation: Green Revolution side effects: Punjab's water table fell dramatically, mono-cropping reduced diversity, excess chemicals polluted, benefits unequal (Punjab/Haryana vs eastern India).

questions.question: A farmer wants to improve milk yield sustainably. Best approach?
options: Cross-breed local cows with high-yield exotic breeds, improve feed quality, veterinary care, clean housing
questions.explanation: Scientific dairy management: cross-breeding (local disease resistance + exotic high yield), balanced cattle feed, regular vaccination, proper housing, clean milking practices.

questions.question: Post-harvest loss in India is approximately what percentage of food grains?
options: 4–6% (official estimates) up to 30% in some commodities like fruits/vegetables
Zero — all grain is stored well
questions.explanation: India loses 4–6% of food grains post-harvest (official). Fruits/vegetables: up to 25–40% loss. Total economic loss: ₹92,000+ crore annually (ICAR estimates).

questions.question: Why is vermicompost considered superior to chemical fertilizers for sustainable farming?
options: It improves soil structure, provides balanced slow-release nutrients, promotes soil microbes, is free from pollution
questions.explanation: Vermicompost: improves soil aeration and water retention (structure benefit), slow-release balanced NPK + micronutrients, promotes beneficial microorganisms, zero chemical pollution.

questions.question: What is the role of micro-organisms in agriculture?
options: Decompose organic matter (release nutrients), fix nitrogen (Rhizobium), and some cause diseases requiring management
questions.explanation: Microorganisms in agriculture: beneficial — decomposers (nutrient recycling), nitrogen fixers (Rhizobium, Azotobacter), mycorrhizae (root helpers). Harmful — fungal/bacterial crop diseases.

questions.question: Food chain scenario: Paddy → Rat → Snake → Hawk. If pesticide kills all rats, what happens?
options: No effect on the food chain
Snake population crashes → hawk population crashes; unchecked paddy pests may increase elsewhere
Hawk population increases without snake competition
Only paddy benefits with no other effects
questions.explanation: Removing rats: snakes starve → snake population falls → hawk population falls. Ecological cascade. Also, other paddy pests (not rats) may increase. Pesticides have chain effects.

questions.question: Why are GM crops controversial in India?
options: Concerns about biodiversity loss, corporate seed control, unknown health effects, contamination of non-GM crops
They always fail to increase yield
The government supports them fully without debate
questions.explanation: GM crop controversy: monopoly of seed companies (Monsanto/Bayer), risk to local biodiversity, unknown long-term health effects, cross-pollination with non-GM crops, farmer dependence on company seeds.

questions.question: What is the connection between animal husbandry and crop farming?
options: Cattle provide draught power (ploughing), manure (fertilizer), and consume crop by-products (straw as feed) — deeply interlinked
questions.explanation: Mixed farming: animals pull ploughs, provide manure for crops, eat crop residues (straw). This circular system reduces input costs and maintains soil fertility — traditional Indian farming.

questions.question: Best summary of crop production and management:
options: It is only about sowing and harvesting
A systematic series of agricultural practices — from soil prep to storage — integrated with animal husbandry, modern technology, and sustainability principles for food security
questions.explanation: Week synthesis: Crop production = integrated system (soil, seed, water, nutrition, pest management, harvest, storage) linked to animal husbandry, technology adoption, and sustainability for India's 1.4 billion people.
